## Goal

One server-enforced switch that keeps every part of the application outside the agreed launch scope unreachable, so a launch without customer accounts and without payments can be proven rather than assumed.

## Context

The application already contains a customer-account surface (registration, sign-in, two-factor, password reset, account pages and the library's own HTTP routes) and a checkout stub. The planned first launch includes none of them. Hiding links is not a control: the routes stay reachable. The independent review's recommendation for the first launch is to disable that surface by an enforced control rather than ship it half-ready, which also keeps several of its findings off the launch critical path.

## Scope

- A single server-side flag, validated at boot like every other setting, with one documented default per environment.
- Every route outside the launch scope answers the same way for an anonymous and for a would-be authenticated caller: no sign-in form, no account page, no library auth endpoint, no checkout stub.
- Links and navigation entries for the disabled areas disappear with the same flag, so the public site has no dead ends.
- Verification outputs that list every route the build exposes and what it answers with the flag on and off.
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` and `docs/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md` state which value each environment uses.

## Out of scope

- Changing how any of the disabled features work.
- Removing their code.
- Content or design changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the flag set for the first launch, every out-of-scope path answers 404 or 410, proven by tests over the full route list, not a sample.
- [ ] With the flag off, the current behaviour is unchanged and the existing suites still pass.
- [ ] No way to reach a disabled area by a direct URL, a form post, a redirect or a cached response.
- [ ] The public pages in scope are unaffected.

## Required tests

- Unit tests for the flag and for the route list.
- A route-level test per disabled area, both flag states.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-003

P0 · Phase A
